key_insight: Andromeda 2 shows that an AI agent can use prior experimental evidence plus lab and computational tools to iteratively design better drug formulations in an autonomous lab. In a matched-budget comparison, it aims to outperform a prior baseline by making formulation development more evidence-driven and efficient.
problem_solved: Finding high-performing self-emulsifying drug delivery system (SEDDS) formulations is slow, costly, and experimentally intensive because the design space is large and success depends on many interacting variables.
method: Reason over structured in-house experimental evidence to guide formulation choices.
Invoke computational and experimental tools in a closed-loop agentic workflow to propose, test, and refine successive batches.
Run the system in a miniaturized automated laboratory under a matched budget and benchmark it against a prior version (Andromeda 1).
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights how agentic systems can combine evidence retrieval, planning, and tool use to solve real-world scientific optimization problems. It suggests a practical path for building more reliable autonomous labs that learn from prior experiments instead of repeatedly exploring blindly.

paper_title: Evidence-Grounded Agentic Formulation Development in an Autonomous Laboratory
paper_authors: Michael M. Craig, Riley J. Hickman, Yingshan Ma, Rémi Piché-Taillefer, Christine Allen
